This module is a pre-completion checklist for regression bisection work: a short set of checks to run before calling a regression bisection task done.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. State assumptions about regression bisection explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
2. Check that regression bisection terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
3. Prefer explicit, readable regression bisection solutions over clever ones that are hard to verify.
4. Validate regression bisection outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
5. Measure before optimizing any regression bisection bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
6. Re-check edge cases relevant to regression bisection (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
7. When multiple regression bisection strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
8. Before starting regression bisection work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
9. Prefer the simplest regression bisection approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.
10. When regression bisection guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
11. Keep regression bisection changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Do not apply generic regression bisection advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Avoid introducing new regression bisection abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not silently drop regression bisection edge cases to make an example look cleaner than the real system.
- Do not skip documenting regression bisection assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
When in doubt, prefer clarity and explicit reasoning about regression bisection over a shortcut that saves a few lines but hides intent.
